For those that do, there is currently no cost to camp, but camping first-come, first served and reservations are not accepted.'

K.A.R. 115-8-9 as amended April 2023, Kansas Register Vol. 42 No. 14 (https://kssos.org/publications/Register/Volume-42/Issues/Issue-14/04-06-23-51015.html), read 2026-11-06: '(a) Camping shall be allowed only in designated areas on department lands and waters ...'; '(c) All campers and camping units at a state fishing lake or wildlife area shall be limited to a stay of not more than seven consecutive days on that department managed land unless otherwise established by posted notice or authorized by written permit from the department. Upon completing seven consecutive days on the same campsite, each person and all property of each person shall be absent from the department-managed area for at least five days.'

values.note: Free, first come; no reservations at Kansas state fishing lakes. Seven consecutive days at a state fishing lake, then five days away (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), amended 2023); a longer stay needs a written KDWP permit.

note: KDWP state fishing lake: an 84-acre clear-water, no-wake lake beside US-166, 16 miles east of Arkansas City. Two primitive camping areas on the north side, Hill Top (on the hill) and Shoreline (by the water), each with a vault toilet; unmarked gravel pull-ins, vehicles on maintained roads only. Boats for fishing only. --Claude
summary: KDWP Cowley page (Wayback 2026-07-12): 84-acre lake, Hill Top + Shoreline primitive camping, vault toilets; free and FCFS; max stay 7 nights (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c), new). Lakefront kept (weakly). Phone missing -> (620) 876-5730. Pin fine. Note cleaned.
flags: WATERFRONT: stored LAKEFRONT kept, but it is a weak keep. KDWP says Shoreline Campground is 'by the water'; on Esri the gravel loop at the stored pin / KDWP's Hill Top point (37.10043,-96.80187) sits 40-60 m from the lake across open grass and a rocky ledge with no road between, a spur off the hilltop vault-toilet loop reaches ~15-30 m from the water, and a gravel lane east of the boat ramp has pull-ins 10-20 m from the water on open ground. There are no marked sites, and KDWP's own Shoreline point (N37 06.170 W96 47.273 = 37.10283,-96.78788) lands on a bare hillside 1.2 km east with no road, and its Shoreline vault toilet (37.11022,-96.79725) 800 m north of the lake, so I could not tie 'Shoreline' to a place. If AWH wants the rule's 'when unsure, go down', LAKEVIEW is the fallback.
PHONE missing (apply.py doesn't write it): propose (620) 876-5730 (KDWP area manager, same number on Google).

PIN 37.10025,-96.80226 is 40 m from KDWP's Hill Top Campground point, on the gravel loop; fine. Google's pin (37.09815,-96.80309) is in the lake. KDWP's Shoreline coordinates look mistyped (above), so no split data; the two areas are at most a few hundred metres apart along the same north shore.
MAX STAY: newly written 7 nights (K.A.R. 115-8-9(c)); the Cowley page posts no other limit. Hookups (none) left as stored; KDWP types both areas 'primitive camping'.
